modules.title: 先用灰块排好位置，再上颜色和字体

items.title: 定位置和大小
items.text: 页头多高、首屏占多大、几张卡片怎么排——这些结构问题在线框阶段确认，改起来只动方框。

items.title: 写占位文字
items.text: 真实文案还没定时，用「一句主标题」「一段说明」这样的占位标注，别为了线框提前编内容。

modules.title: 它不是什么
modules.text: 线框图不是视觉稿：不带颜色、字体和图片，讨论它时别评价「好不好看」。它也不等于需求文档——需求说清「给谁用、要什么」，线框只管「摆在哪」。

lessonPractice.title: AI 问你「首页做成什么样」，你现在只想确定区块位置。下面哪个回答更合适？

options.label: 先画灰色骨架：页头、首屏、卡片、页脚排好位置，颜色之后再说
options.feedback: 对。线框图阶段只定结构，位置确认了再上视觉，要改的也最少。

options.label: 直接给我做一版带渐变和字体的成品，看完再说
options.feedback: 直接上视觉后，改一个区块位置往往连着改颜色、间距和字体；结构没定时这样改最贵。

options.label: 把所有文字内容写好就行，页面怎么排你看着办
options.feedback: 内容固然要先定，但区块位置也需要你确认——「看着办」容易做出和你想法偏差很大的结构。

en.title: The AI asks "what should the homepage look like?" and you only want to settle block positions. Which reply fits?

options.label: Draw a gray skeleton first: header, hero, cards, footer in position; colors later
options.feedback: Correct. The wireframe stage fixes structure only; visuals come after positions are confirmed, with the least to redo.

options.label: Build a finished version with gradients and fonts, and we'll react to it
options.feedback: With visuals already applied, moving one block drags colors, spacing, and fonts along—costliest time to restructure.

options.label: Just write all the copy; arrange the page however you like
options.feedback: Content does come first, but block positions need your confirmation too—"however you like" invites big drift.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 先出首页的线框图：灰色占位块就行，标出页头、首屏、三张能力卡和页脚的位置和大概高度。我确认位置以后，你再上颜色和字体。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Start with a wireframe of the homepage: gray placeholder blocks marking header, hero, three cards, and footer with rough heights. Once I confirm the positions, apply colors and fonts.

learning.assumes: You have seen a floor plan or sketched a rough page layout.
learning.outcome: You can tell the wireframe stage from visual design, and ask an AI for a structural draft before styling.

items.title: Positions and sizes
items.text: Header height, hero footprint, card arrangement—structure questions get settled here, and changes only move boxes.

items.title: Placeholder text
items.text: Until real copy exists, label blocks as "one headline" or "one paragraph" instead of inventing content for the skeleton.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: A wireframe is not a visual mockup: no colors, fonts, or images, so don't judge it by looks. It is also not a requirements doc—requirements say "for whom and what," the wireframe says "where." With an AI, split the rounds: confirm structure on the wireframe, then ask for visuals.

distinctions.label: PRD
distinctions.text: {c:prd} states for whom and what; {c:wireframe} only shows where each block sits on the page.

distinctions.label: Visual hierarchy
distinctions.text: {c:visual-hierarchy} decides which block reads first; {c:wireframe} is the gray skeleton you arrange before styling.
